master.title: Skopje - Latest media update
master.content:
Latest media update

Skopje, 28 Oct 2024

 

 

Construction works kick off on the Gostivar Bukojcani section, part of Corridor 8

The Construction works started today on the Gostivar-Bukojcani section which is the most complicated part of Corridor 8, which is being built by the Bechtel and Enka consortium, a section that should be 30 kilometres long.

Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski indicated at today's event that after two years of the previous government's promises, it can be seen that work is being done on Corridor 8 on the ground, noting that he wants to see Macedonia as the main transport, railway and gas pipeline crossroads in the region. As the Prime Minister said, the intensification of the work started from the first contact with the management of the company "Bechtel and Enka" in Washington during the NATO Summit. DPM and Minister of Transport, Aleksandar Nikoloski said that after 50 years, the construction of the highway Gostivar-Bukojcani-Kicevo, the most difficult route of the highway Corridor 8 in the west, which means that the trip from Skopje to Ohrid will take about an hour and a half. American Ambassador Aggeler was also on the field. According to her, what is seen on the ground is another proof of the excellent partnership between the USA and Macedonia.

 

The continuation of the works on Corridor 8 even by the Government without ethnic legitimacy proves our fair and visionary policy, the Democratic Union for Integration (DUI) assessed.

 

  Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski spoke with the Bulgarian GERB party leader Boyko Borisov by phone today and wished him a stable government that would remove the obstacles that slow down the Macedonian path to the EU.

   Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski today told reporters it is likely that a working version of a legislation on reforming security structures by merging the National Security Agency and the Intelligence Agency will be drafted by early next year. The reform is in line with practices in NATO member nations.   This serious reform is necessary because it is an established practice in the NATO members. The experiences from some of these countries, for example the United States and Croatia, could be beneficial in the process of reforming the security sector, he stated. According to him, the announced reform has upset secret service installations in the opposition parties that have been in top posts for years and decades. They are upset because all scandals and misuse done during their terms will come to light slowly but surely, the PM said.

Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski claims that the National Security Agency (NSA) director, Bojan Hristovski, meets the requirements according to the law. He called on the Anti-Corruption Commission to state its decision on this case as soon as possible following accusations from the opposition that Hristovski does not meet the requirements to be the NSA director.

"I claim that all requirements according to the law have been met. The only authority that should say whether those requirements are met is the Anti-Corruption Commission, and I call on the commission to look into this case as soon as possible. I am convinced that he meets the requirements. Surely we will not let something like that happen. The document has been issued since 2022, whether that Agency existed in the meantime is a completely different question," Mickoski said following Sunday's accusations from the opposition SDSM that Hristovski's English language certificate has been forged.

Mickoski said that if any lapse is found in the case of Hristovski, he will demand responsibility. On Sunday, the opposition SDSM reiterated the demand for resignation of the NSA director because, the party said, he had a false English language certificate.

In addition to a resignation from Hristovski, SDSM demands immediate response from the Anti-Corruption Commission as well as resignation and responsibility on the part of Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski for partisanship of institutions by appointing persons of impaired integrity and no qualifications. Bulgaria's Faktor news said its journalists conducted checks that showed there is no authorized language centre in Plovdiv for issuing the internationally recognized TOEFL certificate, and according to the register of schools in Bulgaria, there is not even a school with the name Language School Julia Co.

 

DUI leader Ahmeti sends letters to IC and to PM Mickoski

After sending a letter to several European leaders and international representatives yesterday in which he expressed concern about the non-observance of the Ohrid Agreement, the leader of DUI Ali Ahmeti, today sent a similar letter to the Prime Minister and leader of VMRO-DPMNE, Hristijan Mickoski. In the letter, Ahmeti voices concern over the decision of the Constitutional Court for the abolition of the balancer and for a possible revision of the Law on languages and their impact on inter-ethnic relations in the country. The leader of DUI warns of serious consequences in case of, as he says, any new violation of inter-ethnic relations and non-respect of the Ohrid Agreement. Today, Prime Minister Mickoski said that he hadn't received the letter yet, but that he would pay attention to it as well as to all letters coming from citizens. First DPM Izet Mexhiti qualified this letter as pointless talks .

The Minister from ZNAM on public administration Goran Minchev sees political populism in the letters of Ahmeti in the absence of unity and vision in DUI. He believes that there is no danger to the security of the state, and the remarks of DUI about the decisions of the Constitutional Court are, in his opinion, unfounded.

Minchev today stated there are two ways for incorporating ethnic diversity and equal employment opportunity measures into the national legislation: one is as part of the draft Law on Civil Servants, the draft Law on Public Sector Employees, and the draft Law on Professional Development and Training of Public Sector Employees; the other is through drafting a separate bill on equitable ethnic representation in hiring governmental workers, Minister of Public Administration Goran Minchev said Monday, adding that the Ministry of Public Administration was not working on any of these at the moment.

According to Minister Minchev, adopting any affirmative action policies should not be rushed. Minchev was answering reporters' questions after the fourth and final public debate on the draft Law on Civil Servants, the draft Law on Public Sector Employees, and the draft Law on Professional Development and Training of Public Sector Employees.

 

Only 46 percent of children part of pre-school education, further efforts needed in sector

Further efforts are needed for the development of pre-school education and the country must invest in both access and quality, said Steffen Hudolin, Head of Cooperation in the EU Delegation to the country, at Monday's final conference of a project on raising the quality of pre-school education and care. "Regarding access, despite the recent progress of enrolment of children aged 3-6, the 46-percent mark is still very low, considering that the EU has set the goal at 96 percent. We are aware that children from higher-income families will most probably go to pre-school. Only four percent of Roma children attend pre-school education, and it should be accessible to all, regardless of the parents' income," said Hudolin. He added that kindergartens should have an opening for all children, coming from both urban and rural environments. "This does not mean that new facilities are a must, but a revision of the existing ones in order to optimise the network of schools and kindergartens. Rational numbers should be the priority, because if we have too many children in classrooms then learning is much harder, and if the groups are smaller, teachers can work individually with children," said Hudolin.

 

Platform: 100% Dedicated to You - Developing cultural tourism, new education laws, capital investments in sport

A new program on tourism, with focus on cultural tourism, new education laws, including a law on textbooks, construction of 30 sports halls, capital investments in sports, as well as financial resources and assistance for clubs, federations and individuals are part of the priority activities that the ministers announced in their address at the event for the "Platform: 100% Dedicated to You," held in the Government on Monday, on the topic of "Measures and policies for the development of education, culture, tourism, and sport."

 

ZELS President Gjorgjievski: Karpos Mayor remains in ZELS

After the meeting with the mayor of Karposh, Stevco Jakimovski today, the president of the Association of Local Self-Government Units, Orce Gjorgjievski informed that Jakimovski remains in ZELS.

He said that ZELS is united and that in the coming period it will continue with intensive communication with the Municipality of Strumica, as well as that it will mediate between Karposh, Strumica and the central government.

 

 

Best,

 

Ajla
